whatIReported: Twenty-three of the 129 current GameTests have never been executed, derived by comparing the 129 names in the source against the 109 names in the newest full results file.
theFlaw: The comparison treated a renamed test as a new one. Renaming a case changes its name in the source, so it looks absent from an older results file even though the same test ran under its old name.

whatActuallyHappenedInOneClass.renameCommit: b90f5fc, 2026-10-06, whose message is 'drive arch-preparation threading tests from a real failure path' and whose diff shows two lines removed and two added with the same signatures but different names, plus one genuinely new case
whatActuallyHappenedInOneClass.correctCount: One never-run test in this class, not three - two are renames and the third, absentDurableProofKeepsGatePendingWithoutThrowingOrAcknowledging, is new.

theOtherFiveClassesAreUnaffected: BiomeWriterGameTests, LifecycleGameTests, NegotiatedGateGameTests, PaletteGameTests and SiteRuntimeIndexGameTests each had zero tests in the 10-03 results under any name, so for them absence really does mean never run.
correctedCount: 21 rather than 23: 23 minus the two renames.
whatRemainsTrue: The substantive point stands - a group of tests has never executed, their results.xml check against six named classes is still the right verification, and none carries a stale corridor baseline. Only the number moves.
lesson: A name-based comparison cannot distinguish a test that was renamed from one that was added. Distinguishing them needs the rename to be visible, which means looking at history rather than at two snapshots.
